summary: This experimental memo defines a new IP option and ICMP message type that does what traceroute does, showing the path packets take, but with fewer packets and faster completion. It is historic and was replaced by RFC 6814.

eli5.summary: To see the path a letter takes, the usual way sends many test letters. This idea used a special marker so one letter could report its whole trip. It is now historic.

questions: how does ip traceroute option work
what is the difference between standard and ip traceroute
subtitle: A faster way to trace the path packets take through the Internet.

tldr.problem: The existing traceroute tool works but sends 2n packets (where n is the number of hops) and takes time to probe each hop separately, and it only traces the outbound path.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC defines a new IP option and ICMP message type that let a single packet carry path information as it travels, so routers send detailed trace reports to the originator without needing separate probe packets for each hop.
tldr.outcome: This RFC was an experimental proposal that did not gain adoption. Modern traceroute implementations use different approaches. The RFC is now Historic and was replaced by RFC 6814.

today: RFC 1393 is Historic and was superseded by RFC 6814. While the proposal was sound, it did not gain adoption. Modern systems use various approaches to trace paths, including standard traceroute variants, MTR (My Traceroute), and network telemetry systems. The RFC's efficiency gains did not overcome the barrier of requiring router support.

sections.title: The Traceroute Problem
sections.content:
The standard traceroute tool probes each hop by sending packets with Time To Live (TTL) values of 1, 2, 3, and so on, collecting ICMP TTL Exceeded messages to map the path. This approach has drawbacks: it generates 2n packets (two per hop), takes time to probe each hop sequentially, can see the path change during the run, and does not trace the return path to the source.

This RFC proposes an alternative method using a dedicated IP option and ICMP message type specifically designed for tracing, which would use only n+1 packets and provide information about both the outbound and return paths, plus details about link speeds and MTUs at each hop.
sections.eli5: Traceroute the old way is slow because you have to drop a test packet for each step. This paper suggests marking one packet so every hop reports back with what it sees.

sections.title: The Traceroute Option and ICMP Message
sections.content:
The proposal adds a new IP Traceroute option (number 18, class 2 for debugging and measurement) to be carried in the outbound packet. This option contains an ID number (to match responses), the originator's IP address, and two hop count fields: Outbound Hop Count (OHC) for the forward path and Return Hop Count (RHC) for the return path. When set, RHC is initialized to 0xFFFF to distinguish outbound from return packets.

Each router that processes the packet sends an ICMP Traceroute message (type 30) back to the originator with the IP header fields copied from the option, plus the measured output link speed (in octets per second) and MTU of the link on which the packet will be sent. This information helps diagnose path quality and fragmentation issues.
sections.eli5: The special marker tells routers to send back a report, and the report includes the speed and size of the connection they're about to use.

sections.title: Protocol Operation
sections.content:
The originator sends a packet (often an ICMP Echo Request) with the IP Traceroute option set, initializing OHC to 0 and RHC to 0xFFFF. Each router along the path that implements this option increments OHC (for outbound packets) or RHC (for return packets) and sends an ICMP Traceroute message to the originator. The destination node copies the option into the reply packet and sets RHC to 0, so the return path can also be traced.

Unlike standard traceroute, the hop counts in the ICMP Traceroute messages provide information about lost responses: if messages show OHC values 4 and 6, the hop count of 5 was lost. This allows the originator to determine the exact path length and detect packet loss.
sections.eli5: Routers count themselves as they pass the packet, and each one sends a message back telling how many routers it has seen so far.

sections.title: Benefits and Trade-offs
sections.content:
The main advantages over standard traceroute are efficiency (n+1 packets instead of 2n), speed (only one pass needed), independence from path changes during the run, and visibility into both outbound and return paths. The method also provides link speed and MTU information directly from each hop.

The main disadvantage is that the traceroute function must be implemented in routers, whereas standard traceroute requires no special router support—it relies only on the existing TTL Exceeded mechanism. This makes deployment dependent on router vendor support and upgrade cycles. The RFC notes this would be more easily ported to a new IP version than the TTL-based approach.
sections.eli5: This is faster but only works if routers are updated to support it. The old way works everywhere because it uses something routers already do.

left.title: Standard traceroute
left.desc: Send multiple probe packets with increasing TTL, receive error replies for each hop.

right.title: IP Traceroute option
right.desc: Send one marked packet; each router reports back directly.
